new_symbol_range_suggestions.amplitude_softening_gain: positive and small to moderate; zero recovers the parent law, while order-unity values give observable extra wake softening at moderate to large |theta| without reversing the restoring torque

derivation_notes: The parent wake-softening law is refined by allowing the same excess wake to weaken restoring torque more strongly when the pendulum is farther from the bottom position. Using 1 - cos(theta) preserves even symmetry in deflection, vanishes in the small-angle limit, and stays bounded over the admissible sub-rotation regime.
change_summary: The restoring denominator now depends on both wake_intensity and deflection amplitude through an amplitude-dependent coefficient. This creates extra flattening of acceleration versus theta at large |theta| under similar wake conditions, while reducing continuously to the parent when amplitude_softening_gain is zero.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The aerodynamic-stiffness correction multiplies the restoring torque through a denominator depending only on Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0), independent of angular excursion magnitude.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At larger deflections the body presents a different effective incidence to the surrounding separated flow, so the same wake state produces a stronger normal-force-induced reduction of restoring torque than near the bottom position.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set amplitude_softening_gain to zero, or take the small-angle limit theta -> 0 so that 1 - cos(theta) -> 0.

response_change.parent_relation: The wake-softened restoring term scales as sin(theta) divided by a wake-only factor, so at fixed wake_intensity the ratio of restoring acceleration to sin(theta) is independent of deflection amplitude.
response_change.child_relation: Make the wake-induced restoring softening itself amplitude dependent, so the effective reduction grows with both wake_intensity and deflection magnitude; at fixed wake_intensity, larger |theta| experiences disproportionately more restoring weakening than smaller |theta|.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding wake_intensity and omega near the same values across samples, the child predicts a smaller-magnitude restoring contribution at larger |theta| than the parent's single wake gain allows, producing extra flattening of the acceleration-versus-theta curve at large deflection.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when wake_intensity exceeds ambient by order-unity or modestly above and trajectories reach moderate to large deflections, so 1 - cos(theta) is non-negligible while remaining below full-rotation energy.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate versus larger deflection segments at similar wake_intensity already reveal extra flattening of restoring acceleration; in holdout, the same interaction extends to stronger wake episodes without changing sign symmetry or periodicity.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the amplitude-dependent softening coefficient tends to zero, or in the small-angle limit theta -> 0 where 1 - cos(theta) vanishes to leading order.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: deflection-dependent wake softening of gravitational restoring torque
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: At larger deflections the body presents a different effective incidence to the surrounding separated flow, so the same wake state produces a stronger normal-force-induced reduction of restoring torque than near the bottom position.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the restoring coefficient now varies with theta through a bounded nonlinear state function, changing the curvature of the target mapping rather than simply rescaling it.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Wake-induced restoring softening depends only on wake excess and uses one shared gain across all deflection amplitudes.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Wake-induced restoring softening depends on wake excess and is strengthened at larger angular excursions through an amplitude-dependent coefficient.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: -(mass * gravity * center_of_mass_distance / moment_of_inertia) * sin(theta) / (1 + aerodynamic_stiffness_gain * Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0)) - (damping_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * omega - (quadratic_drag_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * wake_intensity * omega * Abs(omega)
evolution_contract.after_fragment: -(mass * gravity * center_of_mass_distance / moment_of_inertia) * sin(theta) / (1 + aerodynamic_stiffness_gain * (1 + amplitude_softening_gain * (1 - cos(theta))) * Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0)) - (damping_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * omega - (quadratic_drag_coefficient / moment_of_inertia) * wake_intensity * omega * Abs(omega)
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set amplitude_softening_gain = 0, or take theta -> 0 so that 1 - cos(theta) -> 0 and the denominator reverts to the parent form to leading order.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compared at similar wake_intensity and omega, normalized restoring acceleration is no longer a function of wake_intensity alone: it decreases further with increasing deflection_strength = 1 - cos(theta), giving visibly more flattened acceleration-versus-theta behavior at large |theta| while matching the parent near small angles or wake_intensity near 1.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of aerodynamic_stiffness_gain in the parent cannot simultaneously match weak softening at small |theta| and stronger softening at large |theta| under the same wake_intensity, because the parent mapping is separable as sin(theta) times a wake-only denominator and therefore lacks the required theta-wake interaction.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when wake_intensity exceeds ambient by order-unity or modestly above and trajectories reach moderate to large deflections, so 1 - cos(theta) is non-negligible while remaining below full-rotation energy.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate versus larger deflection segments at similar wake_intensity already reveal extra flattening of restoring acceleration; in holdout, the same interaction extends to stronger wake episodes without changing sign symmetry or periodicity.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the amplitude-dependent softening coefficient tends to zero, or in the small-angle limit theta -> 0 where 1 - cos(theta) vanishes to leading order.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes wake-induced restoring softening is controlled only by wake_intensity and not by deflection amplitude, imposing one shared wake gain across small- and large-angle motion.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The aerodynamic-stiffness correction multiplies the restoring torque through a denominator depending only on Max(wake_intensity - 1, 0), independent of angular excursion magnitude.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: At larger deflections the body presents a different effective incidence to the surrounding separated flow, so the same wake state produces a stronger normal-force-induced reduction of restoring torque than near the bottom position.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's wake-softening law rather than add a wholly new process. The parent already includes a wake-dependent restoring correction, but it uses a single gain on wake_excess for all deflections. Varying theta along trajectories while holding the same parameter set and comparing intervals with similar wake_intensity and omega, the parent predicts that restoring acceleration normalized by sin(theta) depends only on wake_intensity. The child would instead introduce an interaction between theta and wake_intensity, so large-excursion states show additional restoring softening beyond what the same wake level causes near small excursion. This is scientifically admissible because aerodynamic normal-force effects generally depend on orientation relative to the flow and therefore need not remain proportional to a wake-only scalar. The effect is observable only when both wake_excess and deflection are appreciable; near small angles or wake_intensity near 1 the refinement collapses toward the parent and may be hard to distinguish. A single refit of the parent gain cannot reproduce both weak softening at small |theta| and stronger softening at large |theta| under the same wake_intensity because its mapping is separable in sin(theta) times a wake-only factor.

scenario_text: A rigid pendulum swings about a fixed, frictionless pivot under uniform gravity. Its angular position and angular velocity evolve together from independently varied initial conditions, and the target is the instantaneous angular acceleration along each trajectory. The benchmark should recover the nonlinear restoring effect across both small and large deflections while remaining below the full-rotation energy threshold.
